purpose: Preserve globally balanced weak-region investigations that must not be coerced into territorial-practice claims when the evidence supports only network participation, ambiguous status, or incomplete attribution.

candidates.reason: Specialist scholarship securely documents an eighth-century Ibāḍī trans-Saharan slave traffic drawing enslaved people from the Bilād al-Sūdān, and specifically notes Zaghāwa among peoples transported as slaves by Berber traders. Other early Arabic traditions also report slave tribute at Kawār. This supports a bounded external/network participation research lane but does not by itself establish a territorial slavery P-level for Kanem, Zaghāwa territory, Kawār, Ghana/Wagadu, or West/Central Africa generally.

sources.title: Berbers and Blacks: Ibāḍī Slave Traffic in Eighth-Century North Africa
sources.author: Elizabeth Savage
sources.role: specialist synthesis of the early central-Saharan slave traffic
sources.locator: article argument and note 23 citing al-Yaʿqūbī on Zaghāwa transported as slaves
sources.limitation: The article establishes slave traffic and merchant networks; origin, capture, tribute and sale evidence must remain distinct from territorial-practice prevalence inside southern polities.

rejected_inferences: Do not infer a Kanem/Bornu territorial slavery P-level from the transport of Zaghāwa persons.
Do not treat slave tribute reported at Kawār as proof of uniform slavery practice across the central Sudan.
Do not map all Bilād al-Sūdān as a slave-supplying territory.
Do not convert trans-Saharan trade volume or merchant wealth into territorial prevalence.
candidates.next_evidence_needed: Source-native or specialist evidence tied to a bounded southern polity/place that establishes enslaved status, ownership, alienability, labour or recurrent local enslavement independently of long-distance export. A future external-participation loader should preserve the current traffic evidence without routing it through TERRITORIAL_PRACTICE_CLAIM.

candidates.reason: The accepted staged case is deliberately site-bounded at Songo Mnara. Wider medieval Swahili scholarship and travel accounts attest slavery/slave trade in parts of the coast, but the present batch does not establish one uniform P-level from Somalia to Mozambique.
rejected_inferences: Do not turn one archaeological site's evidence into a coast-wide prevalence classification.
Do not infer local slave use mechanically from participation in Indian Ocean trade.
Do not merge fifteenth-century archaeology with later plantation/export systems.
candidates.next_evidence_needed: Additional independently reviewed site- or polity-specific cases with explicit temporal bounds before any broader regional synthesis.

candidates.reason: The corpus securely supports recurrent captive-taking, but specialist scholarship stresses varied prisoner outcomes and archaeological ambiguity. The staged claim therefore uses captive_taking_incorporation rather than slavery_enslavement.
rejected_inferences: Captive imagery is not a count of enslaved persons.
A depicted prisoner is not automatically an enslaved person.
Tribute, corvée, dependent communities and captive status must not be collapsed into slavery.

candidates.reason: Indigenous accounts and modern scholarship support a hereditary, segregated dependent status, but kauwā is context-sensitive and should not be translated mechanically as chattel slavery in every source.
rejected_inferences: Do not classify all service to aliʻi as kauwā status.
Do not use the later unified Kingdom of Hawaiʻi as the political geometry for the whole pre-1800 archipelago.
Do not infer demographic importance from institutional structure.

candidates.reason: The slavery claim derives from exogenous Chinese textual traditions whose political-geographic descriptions are historically important but not a sufficiently precise polygon authority for the full 228-500 interval.
rejected_inferences: Do not map modern Cambodia or Vietnam as Funan.
Do not assume one maximum-extent Funan reconstruction remained valid across the claim interval.
Do not count repeated later Chinese textual transmission as independent evidence automatically.
